```{r}
#| label: setup
#| code-summary: "Load libraries and data"

library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(conflicted)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(DHARMa)
library(emmeans)
library(kableExtra)
# car, nlme, reactable, htmltools are called via :: only (no attach, no conflicts)

conflicts_prefer(
    dplyr::filter, dplyr::select, dplyr::rename, dplyr::lag,
    lmerTest::lmer, .quiet = TRUE
)

# Reproducibility: a fixed global seed plus deterministic Monte-Carlo quantiles
# for emmeans multivariate-t contrasts (otherwise the p-values vary).
GLOBAL_SEED <- 42L
DHARMA_SEED <- 42L
set.seed(GLOBAL_SEED)
emmeans::emm_options(rng.seed = GLOBAL_SEED)

stat_data_dir    <- here("statistical_analysis", "data")
stat_results_dir <- here("results", "statistical_analysis")
if (!dir.exists(stat_data_dir)) {
    stop("Analysis data not found at ", stat_data_dir)
}
dir.create(stat_results_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Read one per-analysis data table (one row per clone / brain / cell).
read_stat <- function(name) {
    readr::read_csv(file.path(stat_data_dir, name), show_col_types = FALSE)
}

# Write one result table to results/statistical_analysis/.
write_result <- function(x, name) {
    df <- as.data.frame(x)
    rn <- rownames(df)
    if (!is.null(rn) && !identical(rn, as.character(seq_len(nrow(df))))) {
        df <- tibble::rownames_to_column(df, "term")
    }
    readr::write_csv(df, file.path(stat_results_dir, name))
    invisible(df)
}

minimal_tbl <- function(df) {
    df %>%
        kbl(align = "c") %>%
        kable_styling(
            bootstrap_options = c("condensed", "bordered"),
            full_width        = FALSE,
            position          = "left"
        )
}

fmt_p <- function(p, digits = 2) {
    if (is.na(p)) return("NA")
    if (p < 0.001) {
        sci   <- formatC(p, format = "e", digits = digits - 1)
        parts <- strsplit(sci, "e")[[1]]
        exp   <- as.integer(parts[2])
        return(paste0(trimws(parts[1]), " \\times 10^{", exp, "}"))
    }
    as.character(signif(p, max(digits, 2)))
}

sig_stars <- function(p, na_as = "") {
    case_when(
        is.na(p)  ~ na_as,
        p < 0.001 ~ "***",
        p < 0.01  ~ "**",
        p < 0.05  ~ "*",
        TRUE      ~ "ns"
    )
}

sig_tbl <- function(df) {
    sig_col <- intersect(c("sig", "sig_label"), names(df))[1]
    if (is.na(sig_col)) return(minimal_tbl(df))

    sig_vals <- df[[sig_col]]
    rows_3 <- which(sig_vals == "***")
    rows_2 <- which(sig_vals == "**")
    rows_1 <- which(sig_vals == "*")

    df[[sig_col]] <- dplyr::case_when(
        sig_vals == "***" ~ kableExtra::cell_spec(sig_vals, bold = TRUE, color = "#1a7b1a"),
        sig_vals == "**"  ~ kableExtra::cell_spec(sig_vals, bold = TRUE, color = "#2d8a2d"),
        sig_vals == "*"   ~ kableExtra::cell_spec(sig_vals, bold = TRUE, color = "#5aaa5a"),
        sig_vals == "ns"  ~ kableExtra::cell_spec(sig_vals, color = "#999999"),
        TRUE ~ sig_vals
    )

    tbl <- df %>%
        kbl(align = "c", escape = FALSE) %>%
        kable_styling(
            bootstrap_options = c("condensed", "bordered"),
            full_width        = FALSE,
            position          = "left"
        )

    if (length(rows_3) > 0) tbl <- tbl %>% row_spec(rows_3, background = "#c8e6c9")
    if (length(rows_2) > 0) tbl <- tbl %>% row_spec(rows_2, background = "#def0de")
    if (length(rows_1) > 0) tbl <- tbl %>% row_spec(rows_1, background = "#f0faf0")

    tbl
}
```

---

## Fig 1B: NSC lineage size

NSC lineage size (progeny per NSC clone) is compared across Control,
Complex I, and Complex V RNAi, one clone per row. Two mosaic systems affect
different fractions of NSCs and are analysed as separate models:

- **Most NSCs affected:** `worniu-GAL4, Tub-FRT-Stop-FRT-GFP`
- **Few NSCs affected:** `Actin-FRT-Stop-FRT-GAL4, UAS-mCD8-GFP`

Brains are the biological replicate and enter each panel's model as a random
intercept:

`lineage_size ~ rnai + (1 | brain_uid)`

Complex I and Complex V RNAi are each compared to the panel-matched Control RNAi,
with a multivariate-$t$ adjustment across the two comparisons within a panel.

```{r}
#| label: fig1b-load-data
#| code-summary: "Load Fig 1B lineage-size data and tabulate clones and brains per group"
#| output: true

fig1b_df <- read_stat("fig_01b_lineage_size.csv") %>%
    filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
    transmute(
        lineage_size = value,
        genotype     = genotype,
        panel = factor(
            if_else(panel_side == "left", "Most NSCs affected", "Few NSCs affected"),
            levels = c("Most NSCs affected", "Few NSCs affected")
        ),
        rnai      = factor(rnai, levels = c("Control", "Complex I", "Complex V")),
        brain_uid = factor(replicate_id)
    )

fig1b_df %>%
    group_by(panel, rnai) %>%
    summarise(
        n_clones = n(),
        n_brains = n_distinct(brain_uid),
        .groups  = "drop"
    ) %>%
    minimal_tbl()
```

### Diagnostics

```{r}
#| label: fig1b-lme-fit
#| code-summary: "Fit panel-specific linear mixed-effects models"

fig1b_most_df <- fig1b_df %>% filter(panel == "Most NSCs affected")
fig1b_few_df  <- fig1b_df %>% filter(panel == "Few NSCs affected")

fig1b_most_model <- lmerTest::lmer(
    lineage_size ~ rnai + (1 | brain_uid),
    data = fig1b_most_df,
    REML = TRUE
)

fig1b_few_model <- lmerTest::lmer(
    lineage_size ~ rnai + (1 | brain_uid),
    data = fig1b_few_df,
    REML = TRUE
)

summary(fig1b_most_model)
summary(fig1b_few_model)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" collapse="true"}
## Model fit diagnostics with DHARMa

Scaled residuals from 1,000 simulations are tested for uniform distribution
(Kolmogorov–Smirnov), dispersion, and an excess of outliers; all three should be
non-significant for a well-fitting model.

```{r}
#| label: fig1b-dharma
#| code-summary: "Run DHARMa diagnostics"
#| output: true
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

sim_fig1b_most <- DHARMa::simulateResiduals(fig1b_most_model, n = 1000, seed = DHARMA_SEED)
sim_fig1b_few  <- DHARMa::simulateResiduals(fig1b_few_model,  n = 1000, seed = DHARMA_SEED)

plot(sim_fig1b_most)
plot(sim_fig1b_few)

invisible(capture.output(
    fig1b_dharma_tests <- list(
        most_uniformity     = DHARMa::testUniformity(sim_fig1b_most, plot = FALSE),
        most_dispersion     = DHARMa::testDispersion(sim_fig1b_most, plot = FALSE),
        most_outliers = DHARMa::testOutliers(sim_fig1b_most, plot = FALSE),
        few_uniformity      = DHARMa::testUniformity(sim_fig1b_few,  plot = FALSE),
        few_dispersion      = DHARMa::testDispersion(sim_fig1b_few,  plot = FALSE),
        few_outliers  = DHARMa::testOutliers(sim_fig1b_few,  plot = FALSE)
    )
))

fig1b_dharma_tests %>%
    purrr::map_dfr(
        \(t) tibble(statistic = t$statistic, p.value = t$p.value),
        .id = "test"
    ) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)), sig = sig_stars(p.value)) %>%
    minimal_tbl()
```

:::

### Global F-test

Type III ANOVA F-test of the `rnai` term, shown separately for each panel.

```{r}
#| label: fig1b-anova
#| code-summary: "Type III ANOVA"
#| output: true

bind_rows(
    anova(fig1b_most_model, type = "III", ddf = "Satterthwaite") %>%
        as.data.frame() %>%
        tibble::rownames_to_column("term") %>%
        mutate(panel = "Most NSCs affected"),
    anova(fig1b_few_model,  type = "III", ddf = "Satterthwaite") %>%
        as.data.frame() %>%
        tibble::rownames_to_column("term") %>%
        mutate(panel = "Few NSCs affected")
) %>%
    rename(df_num = NumDF, df_den = DenDF, F = `F value`, p.value = `Pr(>F)`) %>%
    select(panel, term, everything()) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)), sig = sig_stars(p.value)) %>%
    sig_tbl()
```

### Complex I and Complex V RNAi vs. Control RNAi, per panel (multivariate-$t$ adjusted)

Estimates are in progeny per NSC lineage. Each RNAi condition is compared to
the panel-matched Control RNAi group.

```{r}
#| label: fig1b-contrasts
#| code-summary: "Complex I and Complex V vs. Control contrasts, per panel (multivariate-$t$ adjusted)"

fig1b_most_em <- emmeans::emmeans(fig1b_most_model, specs = ~ rnai)
fig1b_few_em  <- emmeans::emmeans(fig1b_few_model,  specs = ~ rnai)

fig1b_most_contrasts <- summary(
    emmeans::contrast(
        fig1b_most_em,
        method = "trt.vs.ctrl",
        ref    = "Control",
        adjust = "mvt"
    ),
    infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)
) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    mutate(panel = "Most NSCs affected")

fig1b_few_contrasts <- summary(
    emmeans::contrast(
        fig1b_few_em,
        method = "trt.vs.ctrl",
        ref    = "Control",
        adjust = "mvt"
    ),
    infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)
) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    mutate(panel = "Few NSCs affected")

fig1b_contrast_results <- bind_rows(
    fig1b_most_contrasts,
    fig1b_few_contrasts
) %>%
    select(panel, everything()) %>%
    mutate(sig = sig_stars(p.value))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig1b-contrast-table
#| output: true
#| echo: false

fig1b_contrast_results %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3))) %>%
    sig_tbl()
```

## Fig 1G: NSC proliferation vs. in situ heteroplasmy

EdU-positive progeny count is regressed on *in situ* heteroplasmy
(% mutant mtDNA, from *D. melanogaster* / *D. yakuba* mtDNA smFISH), one
neuroblast per row, across four brains (B1–B4) with brain included as a fixed effect:

`progeny ~ heteroplasmy + brain`

```{r}
#| label: fig1g-load-data
#| code-summary: "Load Fig 1G heteroplasmy/EdU data and summarise per brain"
#| output: true

# In situ heteroplasmy is the D. melanogaster / (D. melanogaster + D. yakuba)
# mtDNA smFISH fraction; one row per scored neuroblast, four brains (B1-B4).
fig1g_df <- read_stat("fig_01g_heteroplasmy.csv") %>%
    transmute(
        progeny      = value,
        het_pct      = heteroplasmy_pct,
        het_fraction = heteroplasmy_fraction,
        d_mel, d_yak,
        brain = factor(brain_label, levels = c("B1", "B2", "B3", "B4"))
    )

stopifnot(nrow(fig1g_df) == 53L)

fig1g_df %>%
    group_by(brain) %>%
    summarise(
        n_neuroblasts = n(),
        het_range     = paste0(round(min(het_pct)), "-", round(max(het_pct)), "%"),
        mean_progeny  = round(mean(progeny), 2),
        .groups       = "drop"
    ) %>%
    minimal_tbl()
```

### Diagnostics

```{r}
#| label: fig1g-lm
#| code-summary: "Fit linear model with brain as a fixed effect"

fig1g_lm <- lm(progeny ~ het_pct + brain, data = fig1g_df)
summary(fig1g_lm)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" collapse="true"}
## Model fit diagnostics with DHARMa

Scaled residuals from 1,000 simulations are tested for uniform distribution (Kolmogorov–Smirnov), dispersion, and an excess of outliers; all three should be non-significant for a well-fitting model.

```{r}
#| label: fig1g-dharma
#| code-summary: "Run DHARMa diagnostics"
#| output: true
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

sim_fig1g <- DHARMa::simulateResiduals(fig1g_lm, n = 1000, seed = DHARMA_SEED)
plot(sim_fig1g)

invisible(capture.output(
    fig1g_dharma_tests <- list(
        uniformity     = DHARMa::testUniformity(sim_fig1g, plot = FALSE),
        dispersion     = DHARMa::testDispersion(sim_fig1g, plot = FALSE),
        outliers = DHARMa::testOutliers(sim_fig1g, plot = FALSE)
    )
))

fig1g_dharma_tests %>%
    purrr::map_dfr(
        \(t) tibble(statistic = t$statistic, p.value = t$p.value),
        .id = "test"
    ) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)), sig = sig_stars(p.value)) %>%
    minimal_tbl()
```

:::

### Global F-test

Type III ANOVA on `progeny ~ heteroplasmy + brain`; the `heteroplasmy` term tests whether *in situ* heteroplasmy predicts progeny count once brain is held fixed.

```{r}
#| label: fig1g-anova
#| code-summary: "Type III ANOVA"
#| output: true

fig1g_anova <- car::Anova(fig1g_lm, type = "III") %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("term") %>%
    rename(df = Df, F = `F value`, p.value = `Pr(>F)`)

fig1g_anova %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)), sig = sig_stars(p.value)) %>%
    sig_tbl()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig1g-anova-stats
#| echo: false
#| output: false
fig1g_het_row   <- fig1g_anova %>% filter(term == "het_pct")
fig1g_het_f     <- signif(fig1g_het_row$F, 3)
fig1g_het_df    <- fig1g_het_row$df
fig1g_het_dfres <- fig1g_lm$df.residual
fig1g_het_p     <- fmt_p(fig1g_het_row$p.value)
```

Heteroplasmy has no significant effect on progeny count once brain is accounted for ($F(`r fig1g_het_df`, `r fig1g_het_dfres`) = `r fig1g_het_f`$, $p = `r fig1g_het_p`$).

## Fig 1P: Mito-XhoI in heteroplasmic and homoplasmic NSC clones

EdU-positive progeny per NSC clone is compared in a 2 × 2 factorial
of mitochondrially targeted transgene (`MitoGFP` control vs. `MitoXho1`) ×
mtDNA background (`Homoplasmic WT` vs. `Heteroplasmic`), one clone per row, with
brain as the biological replicate.

The data are fit with a linear mixed-effects model:

`EdU ~ mito_type * background + (1 | brain_uid)`

Sum-to-zero contrasts are applied to both factors so that each Type III main
effect is marginal to the interaction. `MitoXho1` is then compared to `MitoGFP`
within each mtDNA background, with a multivariate-$t$ adjustment across the two
comparisons.

```{r}
#| label: fig1p-load-data
#| code-summary: "Load Fig 1P heteroplasmic-clone data and tabulate clones and brains per group"
#| output: true

fig1p_df <- read_stat("fig_01p_heteroplasmic_clones.csv") %>%
    filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
    transmute(
        EdU        = value,
        mito_type  = factor(mito_type,        levels = c("MitoGFP", "MitoXho1")),
        background = factor(mtdna_background,  levels = c("Homoplasmic WT", "Heteroplasmic")),
        brain_uid  = factor(replicate_id)
    )

stopifnot(!anyNA(fig1p_df$mito_type), !anyNA(fig1p_df$background))

fig1p_df %>%
    group_by(mito_type, background) %>%
    summarise(
        n_clones = n(),
        n_brains = n_distinct(brain_uid),
        .groups  = "drop"
    ) %>%
    minimal_tbl()
```

### Diagnostics

```{r}
#| label: fig1p-lme
#| code-summary: "Fit clone-level linear mixed-effects model"

contrasts(fig1p_df$mito_type)  <- contr.sum(2)
contrasts(fig1p_df$background) <- contr.sum(2)

fig1p_lme <- lmerTest::lmer(
    EdU ~ mito_type * background + (1 | brain_uid),
    data = fig1p_df,
    REML = TRUE
)
summary(fig1p_lme)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" collapse="true"}
## Model fit diagnostics with DHARMa

Scaled residuals from 1,000 simulations are tested for uniform distribution (Kolmogorov–Smirnov), dispersion, and an excess of outliers; all three should be non-significant for a well-fitting model.

```{r}
#| label: fig1p-dharma
#| code-summary: "Run DHARMa diagnostics"
#| output: true
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

sim_fig1p <- DHARMa::simulateResiduals(fig1p_lme, n = 1000, seed = DHARMA_SEED)
plot(sim_fig1p)

invisible(capture.output(
    fig1p_dharma_tests <- list(
        uniformity     = DHARMa::testUniformity(sim_fig1p, plot = FALSE),
        dispersion     = DHARMa::testDispersion(sim_fig1p, plot = FALSE),
        outliers = DHARMa::testOutliers(sim_fig1p, plot = FALSE)
    )
))

fig1p_dharma_tests %>%
    purrr::map_dfr(
        \(t) tibble(statistic = t$statistic, p.value = t$p.value),
        .id = "test"
    ) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)), sig = sig_stars(p.value)) %>%
    minimal_tbl()
```

The uniformity (KS) test is borderline
($p = `r signif(fig1p_dharma_tests$uniformity$p.value, 2)`$) but not significant,
and the dispersion and outlier tests are not flagged, so the Gaussian
linear mixed-effects model is retained.

:::

### Global F-test

Type III ANOVA (Satterthwaite degrees of freedom) on the two main effects and their interaction.

```{r}
#| label: fig1p-anova
#| code-summary: "Type III ANOVA"
#| output: true

fig1p_anova <- anova(fig1p_lme, type = "III", ddf = "Satterthwaite") %>%
    as.data.frame()

fig1p_anova %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("term") %>%
    rename(df_num = NumDF, df_den = DenDF, F = `F value`, p.value = `Pr(>F)`) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)), sig = sig_stars(p.value)) %>%
    sig_tbl()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig1p-anova-stats
#| echo: false
#| output: false
fig1p_bg_f    <- signif(fig1p_anova["background", "F value"], 3)
fig1p_bg_dfd  <- signif(fig1p_anova["background", "DenDF"], 3)
fig1p_bg_p    <- fmt_p(fig1p_anova["background", "Pr(>F)"])
fig1p_mito_p  <- fmt_p(fig1p_anova["mito_type", "Pr(>F)"])
fig1p_int_p   <- fmt_p(fig1p_anova["mito_type:background", "Pr(>F)"])
```

None of the three terms reach significance: `background` ($F(1, `r fig1p_bg_dfd`) = `r fig1p_bg_f`$, $p = `r fig1p_bg_p`$), `mito_type` ($p = `r fig1p_mito_p`$), and their interaction ($p = `r fig1p_int_p`$).

### MitoXho1 vs. MitoGFP, within each mtDNA background (multivariate-$t$ adjusted)

The two within-background comparisons are taken from the full
`mito_type * background` estimated-marginal-means grid, with a multivariate-$t$
adjustment applied jointly across both.

```{r}
#| label: fig1p-contrasts
#| code-summary: "MitoXho1 vs. MitoGFP within each mtDNA background (multivariate-$t$ adjusted)"
#| output: true

fig1p_em <- emmeans::emmeans(fig1p_lme, ~ mito_type * background)

fig1p_contrast_list <- list(
    "MitoXho1 - MitoGFP | Homoplasmic WT" = c(-1, 1,  0, 0),
    "MitoXho1 - MitoGFP | Heteroplasmic"  = c( 0, 0, -1, 1)
)

fig1p_contrast_results <- emmeans::contrast(
    fig1p_em,
    method = fig1p_contrast_list,
    adjust = "mvt"
) %>%
    summary(infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)), sig = sig_stars(p.value))

fig1p_contrast_results %>%
    sig_tbl()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig1p-contrast-stats
#| echo: false
#| output: false
fig1p_get <- function(bg) fig1p_contrast_results %>% filter(str_detect(contrast, fixed(bg)))
fig1p_homo_est <- fig1p_get("Homoplasmic WT")$estimate
fig1p_homo_p   <- fmt_p(fig1p_get("Homoplasmic WT")$p.value)
fig1p_het_est  <- fig1p_get("Heteroplasmic")$estimate
fig1p_het_p    <- fmt_p(fig1p_get("Heteroplasmic")$p.value)
```

MitoXho1 does not significantly change EdU⁺ progeny count relative to MitoGFP in either the Homoplasmic WT background (`r fig1p_homo_est` progeny, $p = `r fig1p_homo_p`$) or the Heteroplasmic background (`r fig1p_het_est` progeny, $p = `r fig1p_het_p`$).

## Fig 3E & Supp Fig 7J: UCP1 / UCP2 rescue experiment

NSC mitotic index (% pH3⁺Dpn⁺ / Dpn⁺) is compared in a 3 × 3
factorial of RNAi condition (`Control`, `Complex I`, `Complex V`) × UCP
expression (`GFP`, `UCP1`, `UCP2`), one brain per row (n = 6–13 per cell). The
`UCP1` analysis is shown in Fig 3E and the `UCP2` analysis is shown in
Supp Fig 7J; both are analysed
here together. An interaction linear model is fit to the per-brain values:

`Mitotic_index ~ rnai * ucp`

```{r}
#| label: load-ucp-data
#| code-summary: "Load UCP1 / UCP2 rescue data and tabulate brains per cell"
#| output: true

ucp_df <- read_stat("fig_03e_ucp_rescue.csv") %>%
    filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
    transmute(
        Mitotic_index = value,
        ucp  = factor(rescue_transgene, levels = c("GFP", "UCP1", "UCP2")),
        rnai = factor(rnai,             levels = c("Control", "Complex I", "Complex V"))
    )

# Explicit sum-to-zero coding is required for interpretable Type III main
# effects in this unbalanced factorial design.
contrasts(ucp_df$ucp)  <- contr.sum(nlevels(ucp_df$ucp))
contrasts(ucp_df$rnai) <- contr.sum(nlevels(ucp_df$rnai))

ucp_df %>%
    count(rnai, ucp, name = "n_brains") %>%
    minimal_tbl()
```

### Diagnostics

```{r}
#| label: ucp-lm-raw
#| code-summary: "Fit interaction linear model (RNAi × UCP) on per-brain mitotic index"

ucp_lm_raw <- lm(Mitotic_index ~ rnai * ucp, data = ucp_df)
summary(ucp_lm_raw)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" collapse="true"}
## Model fit diagnostics with DHARMa

Scaled residuals from 1,000 simulations are tested for uniform distribution (Kolmogorov–Smirnov), dispersion, and an excess of outliers; all three should be non-significant for a well-fitting model.

```{r}
#| label: ucp-dharma-raw
#| code-summary: "Run DHARMa diagnostics"
#| output: true
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

sim_ucp_raw <- DHARMa::simulateResiduals(ucp_lm_raw, n = 1000, seed = DHARMA_SEED)
plot(sim_ucp_raw)

invisible(capture.output(
    ucp_dharma_tests <- list(
        uniformity     = DHARMa::testUniformity(sim_ucp_raw, plot = FALSE),
        dispersion     = DHARMa::testDispersion(sim_ucp_raw, plot = FALSE),
        outliers = DHARMa::testOutliers(sim_ucp_raw, plot = FALSE)
    )
))

ucp_dharma_tests %>%
    purrr::map_dfr(
        \(t) tibble(statistic = t$statistic, p.value = t$p.value),
        .id = "test"
    ) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)), sig = sig_stars(p.value)) %>%
    minimal_tbl()
```

:::

### Global F-test

Type III ANOVA on `rnai * ucp`:

- `rnai`: whether RNAi knockdown affects mitotic index overall
- `ucp`: whether UCP expression alone has an effect
- `rnai:ucp`: whether the UCP effect differs across RNAi backgrounds

```{r}
#| label: ucp-anova
#| code-summary: "Type III ANOVA"
#| output: true

ucp_anova_type3 <- car::Anova(ucp_lm_raw, type = "III")

ucp_anova_type3 %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("term") %>%
    rename(df = Df, F = `F value`, p.value = `Pr(>F)`) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)), sig = sig_stars(p.value)) %>%
    sig_tbl()
```

```{r}
#| label: ucp-anova-stats
#| echo: false
#| output: false
ucp_av       <- as.data.frame(ucp_anova_type3)
ucp_res_df   <- ucp_av["Residuals", "Df"]
ucp_rnai_f   <- signif(ucp_av["rnai",     "F value"], 3)
ucp_rnai_dfn <- ucp_av["rnai",     "Df"]
ucp_rnai_p   <- fmt_p(ucp_av["rnai",     "Pr(>F)"])
ucp_ucp_f    <- signif(ucp_av["ucp",      "F value"], 3)
ucp_ucp_dfn  <- ucp_av["ucp",      "Df"]
ucp_ucp_p    <- fmt_p(ucp_av["ucp",      "Pr(>F)"])
ucp_int_f    <- signif(ucp_av["rnai:ucp", "F value"], 3)
ucp_int_dfn  <- ucp_av["rnai:ucp", "Df"]
ucp_int_p    <- fmt_p(ucp_av["rnai:ucp", "Pr(>F)"])
```

The RNAi main effect was highly significant ($F(`r ucp_rnai_dfn`, `r ucp_res_df`) = `r ucp_rnai_f`$, $p = `r ucp_rnai_p`$), with knockdown status accounting for the primary variation in mitotic index. The UCP main effect was not significant ($F(`r ucp_ucp_dfn`, `r ucp_res_df`) = `r ucp_ucp_f`$, $p = `r ucp_ucp_p`$), but the interaction was significant ($F(`r ucp_int_dfn`, `r ucp_res_df`) = `r ucp_int_f`$, $p = `r ucp_int_p`$), with the effect of UCP expression varying by RNAi background.

### Within-condition pairwise tests

`UCP1` and `UCP2` vs. their RNAi-matched `GFP` control within each RNAi condition (Dunnett's test, multivariate-$t$ adjustment across the two comparisons per condition). Estimates are in percentage-point units.

```{r}
#| label: ucp-contrasts
#| code-summary: "Marginal means and Dunnett's contrasts (UCP vs. GFP, multivariate-$t$ adjusted)"

ucp_emmeans <- emmeans::emmeans(ucp_lm_raw, ~ ucp | rnai)

ucp_contrasts <- emmeans::contrast(
    ucp_emmeans,
    method = "trt.vs.ctrl",
    ref    = "GFP",
    adjust = "mvt"
)

ucp_contrasts_summary <- summary(ucp_contrasts, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))
```

```{r}
#| label: ucp-contrasts-table
#| output: true
#| echo: false

ucp_contrasts_summary %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)), sig = sig_stars(p.value)) %>%
    sig_tbl()
```

```{r}
#| label: ucp-contrast-stats
#| echo: false
#| output: false
ucp_cs        <- as_tibble(ucp_contrasts_summary)
ucp_ctrl_ci_p <- min(ucp_cs$p.value[ucp_cs$rnai %in% c("Control", "Complex I")])
ucp_cv1       <- ucp_cs %>% filter(rnai == "Complex V", str_detect(as.character(contrast), "UCP1"))
ucp_cv2       <- ucp_cs %>% filter(rnai == "Complex V", str_detect(as.character(contrast), "UCP2"))
ucp_cv1_est   <- signif(ucp_cv1$estimate, 3)
ucp_cv1_p     <- fmt_p(ucp_cv1$p.value)
ucp_cv2_est   <- signif(ucp_cv2$estimate, 3)
ucp_cv2_p     <- fmt_p(ucp_cv2$p.value)
```

Neither UCP had a significant effect in the `Control` or `Complex I` backgrounds (all $p \ge `r fmt_p(ucp_ctrl_ci_p)`$). In the `Complex V` background, both `UCP1` ($+`r ucp_cv1_est`$ pp, $p = `r ucp_cv1_p`$) and `UCP2` ($+`r ucp_cv2_est`$ pp, $p = `r ucp_cv2_p`$) significantly increased mitotic index relative to `GFP`.

### Cross-condition effect comparisons

Following the significant `rnai:ucp` interaction, these difference-in-differences
contrasts test whether the *magnitude* of the UCP rescue effect differs between
the `Complex V` and `Complex I` backgrounds:

- `(UCP1 − GFP | Complex V) − (UCP1 − GFP | Complex I)`
- `(UCP2 − GFP | Complex V) − (UCP2 − GFP | Complex I)`

```{r}
#| label: ucp-direct-interaction-contrasts
#| code-summary: "UCP rescue effect: (multivariate-$t$ adjusted)"

ucp_cell_emmeans <- emmeans::emmeans(ucp_lm_raw, ~ rnai * ucp)

ucp_all_interactions <- emmeans::contrast(
    ucp_cell_emmeans,
    interaction = c("revpairwise", "trt.vs.ctrl"),
    adjust = "none"
)

ucp_direct_interactions <- subset(
    ucp_all_interactions,
    rnai_revpairwise == "Complex V - Complex I"
)

ucp_direct_interactions_summary <- summary(
    ucp_direct_interactions,
    infer = c(TRUE, TRUE),
    adjust = "mvt"
)

ucp_direct_interactions_summary
```

```{r}
#| label: ucp-interaction-table
#| output: true
#| echo: false

ucp_direct_interactions_summary %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)), sig = sig_stars(p.value)) %>%
    sig_tbl()
```

```{r}
#| label: ucp-interaction-stats
#| echo: false
#| output: false
ucp_di     <- as_tibble(ucp_direct_interactions_summary)
ucp_di_u1  <- ucp_di %>% filter(str_detect(as.character(ucp_trt.vs.ctrl), "UCP1"))
ucp_di_u2  <- ucp_di %>% filter(str_detect(as.character(ucp_trt.vs.ctrl), "UCP2"))
ucp_di_u1_est <- signif(ucp_di_u1$estimate, 3)
ucp_di_u1_p   <- fmt_p(ucp_di_u1$p.value)
ucp_di_u2_est <- signif(ucp_di_u2$estimate, 3)
ucp_di_u2_p   <- fmt_p(ucp_di_u2$p.value)
```

A positive estimate indicates a larger rescue effect in `Complex V`. Multivariate-*t* adjustment is applied across the two contrasts. Both contrasts were significant: the `UCP1` rescue effect was `r ucp_di_u1_est` percentage-points larger in `Complex V` than `Complex I` ($p = `r ucp_di_u1_p`$), and the `UCP2` effect was `r ucp_di_u2_est` percentage-points larger ($p = `r ucp_di_u2_p`$).

## Fig 3G: LbNox rescue experiment

NSC mitotic index (% pH3⁺Dpn⁺ / Dpn⁺) is compared in a 3 × 2
factorial of LbNox construct (`Control`, `nlsLbNox`, `mitoLbNox`) × RNAi
background (`Control`, `Complex I`), one brain per row (n = 8–14 per cell). An
interaction linear model is fit to the per-brain values:

`mitotic_index ~ rnai * lbnox`

```{r}
#| label: load-lbnox-data
#| code-summary: "Load Fig 3G LbNox-rescue data and tabulate brains per cell"
#| output: true

# Fig 3G analysing the Control and Complex I backgrounds
lbnox_df <- read_stat("fig_03g_lbnox_rescue.csv") %>%
    filter(!is.na(value), rnai %in% c("Control", "Complex I")) %>%
    transmute(
        mitotic_index = value,
        lbnox = factor(
            if_else(rescue_transgene == "None", "Control", rescue_transgene),
            levels = c("Control", "nlsLbNox", "mitoLbNox")
        ),
        rnai = factor(rnai, levels = c("Control", "Complex I"))
    )

# Sum-to-zero coding for interpretable Type III main effects in this
# unbalanced factorial design.
contrasts(lbnox_df$lbnox) <- contr.sum(nlevels(lbnox_df$lbnox))
contrasts(lbnox_df$rnai)  <- contr.sum(nlevels(lbnox_df$rnai))

lbnox_df %>%
    count(rnai, lbnox, name = "n_brains") %>%
    minimal_tbl()
```

### Diagnostics

```{r}
#| label: lbnox-lm-raw
#| code-summary: "Fit interaction linear model (RNAi × LbNox) on per-brain mitotic index"

lbnox_lm <- lm(mitotic_index ~ rnai * lbnox, data = lbnox_df)
summary(lbnox_lm)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" collapse="true"}
## Model fit diagnostics with DHARMa

Scaled residuals from 1,000 simulations are tested for uniform distribution (Kolmogorov–Smirnov), dispersion, and an excess of outliers; all three should be non-significant for a well-fitting model.

```{r}
#| label: lbnox-dharma
#| code-summary: "Run DHARMa diagnostics"
#| output: true
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

sim_lbnox <- DHARMa::simulateResiduals(lbnox_lm, n = 1000, seed = DHARMA_SEED)
plot(sim_lbnox)

invisible(capture.output(
    lbnox_dharma_tests <- list(
        uniformity     = DHARMa::testUniformity(sim_lbnox, plot = FALSE),
        dispersion     = DHARMa::testDispersion(sim_lbnox, plot = FALSE),
        outliers = DHARMa::testOutliers(sim_lbnox, plot = FALSE)
    )
))

lbnox_dharma_tests %>%
    purrr::map_dfr(
        \(t) tibble(statistic = t$statistic, p.value = t$p.value),
        .id = "test"
    ) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)), sig = sig_stars(p.value)) %>%
    minimal_tbl()
```

:::

### Global F-test

Type III ANOVA on `rnai * lbnox`:

- `rnai`: whether RNAi knockdown affects mitotic index overall
- `lbnox`: whether LbNox expression alone has an effect
- `rnai:lbnox`: whether the LbNox effect differs across RNAi backgrounds

```{r}
#| label: lbnox-anova
#| code-summary: "Type III ANOVA"
#| output: true

lbnox_anova_type3 <- car::Anova(lbnox_lm, type = "III")

lbnox_anova_type3 %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("term") %>%
    rename(df = Df, F = `F value`, p.value = `Pr(>F)`) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)), sig = sig_stars(p.value)) %>%
    sig_tbl()
```

```{r}
#| label: lbnox-anova-stats
#| echo: false
#| output: false
lb_av       <- as.data.frame(lbnox_anova_type3)
lb_res_df   <- lb_av["Residuals",  "Df"]
lb_rnai_f   <- signif(lb_av["rnai",       "F value"], 3)
lb_rnai_dfn <- lb_av["rnai",       "Df"]
lb_rnai_p   <- fmt_p(lb_av["rnai",       "Pr(>F)"])
lb_lb_f     <- signif(lb_av["lbnox",      "F value"], 3)
lb_lb_dfn   <- lb_av["lbnox",      "Df"]
lb_lb_p     <- fmt_p(lb_av["lbnox",      "Pr(>F)"])
lb_int_f    <- signif(lb_av["rnai:lbnox", "F value"], 3)
lb_int_dfn  <- lb_av["rnai:lbnox", "Df"]
lb_int_p    <- fmt_p(lb_av["rnai:lbnox", "Pr(>F)"])
```

The `rnai` main effect was significant ($F(`r lb_rnai_dfn`, `r lb_res_df`) = `r lb_rnai_f`$, $p = `r lb_rnai_p`$), but the `lbnox` main effect was not ($F(`r lb_lb_dfn`, `r lb_res_df`) = `r lb_lb_f`$, $p = `r lb_lb_p`$). The significant interaction ($F(`r lb_int_dfn`, `r lb_res_df`) = `r lb_int_f`$, $p = `r lb_int_p`$) indicates that the effect of LbNox on mitotic index depends on the RNAi background.

### LbNox rescue within each RNAi background (Dunnett-style, multivariate-$t$ adjusted)

`nlsLbNox` and `mitoLbNox` vs. their RNAi-matched `Control` within each RNAi condition (Dunnett's test, multivariate-$t$ adjustment across the two comparisons per condition). Estimates are in percentage-point units.

```{r}
#| label: lbnox-contrasts
#| code-summary: "Marginal means and Dunnett's contrasts (LbNox vs. Control, multivariate-$t$ adjusted)"

lbnox_emmeans <- emmeans::emmeans(lbnox_lm, ~ lbnox | rnai)

lbnox_contrasts <- emmeans::contrast(
    lbnox_emmeans,
    method = "trt.vs.ctrl",
    ref    = "Control",
    adjust = "mvt"
)

lbnox_contrasts_summary <- summary(lbnox_contrasts, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))
```

```{r}
#| label: lbnox-contrasts-table
#| output: true
#| echo: false

lbnox_contrasts_summary %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)), sig = sig_stars(p.value)) %>%
    sig_tbl()
```

```{r}
#| label: lbnox-contrast-stats
#| echo: false
#| output: false
lb_cs     <- as_tibble(lbnox_contrasts_summary)
lb_get    <- function(rnai_lvl, construct) {
    lb_cs %>% filter(as.character(rnai) == rnai_lvl,
                     str_detect(as.character(contrast), construct))
}
lb_ctrl_nls_est  <- signif(lb_get("Control",   "nlsLbNox")$estimate, 3)
lb_ctrl_nls_p    <- fmt_p(lb_get("Control",    "nlsLbNox")$p.value)
lb_ctrl_mito_est <- signif(lb_get("Control",   "mitoLbNox")$estimate, 3)
lb_ctrl_mito_p   <- fmt_p(lb_get("Control",    "mitoLbNox")$p.value)
lb_ci_nls_est    <- signif(lb_get("Complex I", "nlsLbNox")$estimate, 3)
lb_ci_nls_p      <- fmt_p(lb_get("Complex I",  "nlsLbNox")$p.value)
lb_ci_mito_est   <- signif(lb_get("Complex I", "mitoLbNox")$estimate, 3)
lb_ci_mito_p     <- fmt_p(lb_get("Complex I",  "mitoLbNox")$p.value)
```

Within the `Control` RNAi background, both nlsLbNox (`r lb_ctrl_nls_est` pp, $p = `r lb_ctrl_nls_p`$) and mitoLbNox (`r lb_ctrl_mito_est` pp, $p = `r lb_ctrl_mito_p`$) slightly reduced mitotic index relative to no-construct controls. Within the `Complex I` RNAi background, both constructs significantly increased mitotic index: nlsLbNox (`r lb_ci_nls_est` pp, $p = `r lb_ci_nls_p`$) and mitoLbNox (`r lb_ci_mito_est` pp, $p = `r lb_ci_mito_p`$).

### Cross-condition effect comparisons

Following the significant `rnai:lbnox` interaction, these difference-in-differences
contrasts test whether the *magnitude* of the LbNox rescue effect differs between
the `Complex I` and `Control` RNAi backgrounds:

- `(nlsLbNox − Control | Complex I) − (nlsLbNox − Control | Control RNAi)`
- `(mitoLbNox − Control | Complex I) − (mitoLbNox − Control | Control RNAi)`

```{r}
#| label: lbnox-interaction-contrasts
#| code-summary: "LbNox rescue effect: difference-in-differences (multivariate-$t$ adjusted)"

lbnox_cell_emmeans <- emmeans::emmeans(lbnox_lm, ~ rnai * lbnox)

lbnox_all_interactions <- emmeans::contrast(
    lbnox_cell_emmeans,
    interaction = c("revpairwise", "trt.vs.ctrl"),
    adjust = "none"
)

lbnox_direct_interactions <- subset(
    lbnox_all_interactions,
    rnai_revpairwise == "Complex I - Control"
)

lbnox_direct_interactions_summary <- summary(
    lbnox_direct_interactions,
    infer = c(TRUE, TRUE),
    adjust = "mvt"
)

lbnox_direct_interactions_summary
```

```{r}
#| label: lbnox-interaction-table
#| output: true
#| echo: false

lbnox_direct_interactions_summary %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)), sig = sig_stars(p.value)) %>%
    sig_tbl()
```

```{r}
#| label: lbnox-interaction-stats
#| echo: false
#| output: false
lb_di      <- as_tibble(lbnox_direct_interactions_summary)
lb_di_nls  <- lb_di %>% filter(str_detect(as.character(lbnox_trt.vs.ctrl), "nlsLbNox"))
lb_di_mito <- lb_di %>% filter(str_detect(as.character(lbnox_trt.vs.ctrl), "mitoLbNox"))
lb_di_nls_est  <- signif(lb_di_nls$estimate, 3)
lb_di_nls_p    <- fmt_p(lb_di_nls$p.value)
lb_di_mito_est <- signif(lb_di_mito$estimate, 3)
lb_di_mito_p   <- fmt_p(lb_di_mito$p.value)
```

A positive estimate indicates a larger rescue effect in `Complex I` relative to `Control` RNAi. Both difference-in-differences contrasts were significant: the nlsLbNox rescue effect was `r lb_di_nls_est` percentage-points larger in the Complex I background ($p = `r lb_di_nls_p`$), and the mitoLbNox effect was `r lb_di_mito_est` percentage-points larger ($p = `r lb_di_mito_p`$).

## Fig 4C: Glial Inx2 KD and NSC proliferation

EdU-positive progeny per NSC clone is compared across three
populations produced by a bipartite system that drives clonal Complex I RNAi in
scattered NSCs (LexA/LexOp flip-out) while `repo-GAL4` drives the glial transgene
in all glia of the same brain; one clone per row:

- `Luciferase`: Complex I RNAi NSC clones in control glia (Luciferase RNAi)
- `inx2`: Complex I RNAi NSC clones in Inx2-knockdown glia
- `inx2 (not clones)`: wild-type (non-flipped) NSCs in Inx2-knockdown glia,
  measured from the same brains as the `inx2` clones

`inx2` and `inx2 (not clones)` are measured from the *same two physical brains*;
`Luciferase` is an independent set of three unrelated brains.

Because `inx2` and `inx2 (not clones)` are scored on the same brains, those
two conditions share a random-effect group per brain, while the three
`Luciferase` brains form their own groups:

`EdU ~ condition + (1 | brain_uid)`

The `inx2` vs. `inx2 (not clones)` comparison is therefore within-brain and
well replicated at the clone level, whereas comparisons involving `Luciferase`
are limited by the five independent brains available.

```{r}
#| label: inx2-load-data
#| code-summary: "Load Fig 4C inx2 data and tabulate clones and brains per condition"
#| output: true

# `inx2` and `inx2 (not clones)` are scored on the same physical brains and
# share one `replicate_id`, which is used directly as the random-effect group.
inx2_df <- read_stat("fig_04c_inx2_edu.csv") %>%
    filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
    transmute(
        EdU       = value,
        condition = factor(genotype,
                           levels = c("Luciferase", "inx2", "inx2 (not clones)")),
        brain_uid = replicate_id
    )

inx2_df %>%
    group_by(condition) %>%
    summarise(
        n_clones = n(),
        n_brains = n_distinct(brain_uid),
        .groups  = "drop"
    ) %>%
    minimal_tbl()
```

### Diagnostics

```{r}
#| label: inx2-lme
#| code-summary: "Fit clone-level linear mixed-effects model"

inx2_lme <- lmerTest::lmer(
    EdU ~ condition + (1 | brain_uid),
    data    = inx2_df,
    REML    = TRUE,
    control = lme4::lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)

summary(inx2_lme)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" collapse="true"}
## Model fit diagnostics with DHARMa

Scaled residuals from 1,000 simulations are tested for uniform distribution (Kolmogorov–Smirnov), dispersion, and an excess of outliers; all three should be non-significant for a well-fitting model.

```{r}
#| label: inx2-dharma
#| code-summary: "Run DHARMa diagnostics"
#| output: true
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

sim_inx2 <- DHARMa::simulateResiduals(inx2_lme, n = 1000, seed = DHARMA_SEED)
plot(sim_inx2)

invisible(capture.output(
    inx2_dharma_tests <- list(
        uniformity     = DHARMa::testUniformity(sim_inx2, plot = FALSE),
        dispersion     = DHARMa::testDispersion(sim_inx2, plot = FALSE),
        outliers = DHARMa::testOutliers(sim_inx2, plot = FALSE)
    )
))

inx2_dharma_tests %>%
    purrr::map_dfr(
        \(t) tibble(statistic = t$statistic, p.value = t$p.value),
        .id = "test"
    ) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)), sig = sig_stars(p.value)) %>%
    minimal_tbl()
```

:::

```{r}
#| label: inx2-random-effects
#| code-summary: "Variance-components table (between-brain vs. residual)"
#| output: true

vc_inx2 <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(inx2_lme))
vc_inx2$pct <- round(100 * vc_inx2$vcov / sum(vc_inx2$vcov), 1)

vc_inx2[, c("grp", "vcov", "pct")] %>%
    minimal_tbl()
```

### Global F-test

Type III ANOVA (Satterthwaite degrees of freedom) on the `condition` term, testing whether the three populations differ in EdU incorporation.

```{r}
#| label: inx2-anova
#| code-summary: "Type III ANOVA"
#| output: true

anova(inx2_lme, type = "III", ddf = "Satterthwaite") %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("term") %>%
    rename(df_num = NumDF, df_den = DenDF, F = `F value`, p.value = `Pr(>F)`) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)), sig = sig_stars(p.value)) %>%
    sig_tbl()
```

### Inx2 KD effect on CI-deficient and WT NSCs (multivariate-$t$ adjusted)

Estimates are in EdU percentage points.

```{r}
#| label: inx2-contrasts
#| code-summary: "Marginal means and the three inx2 contrasts (multivariate-$t$ adjusted)"
#| output: true

inx2_em <- emmeans::emmeans(inx2_lme, specs = ~ condition)

inx2_contrast_list <- list(
    "inx2 - Luciferase"              = c(-1,  1,  0),
    "inx2 (not clones) - inx2"       = c( 0, -1,  1),
    "inx2 (not clones) - Luciferase" = c(-1,  0,  1)
)

inx2_contrast_results <- emmeans::contrast(inx2_em, method = inx2_contrast_list, adjust = "mvt") %>%
    summary(infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)),
           sig = sig_stars(p.value))

inx2_contrast_results %>%
    sig_tbl()
```

The `inx2 (not clones) - inx2` contrast is a within-brain comparison (both
measured from the same 2 physical brains) and is well powered (df ≈ 35);
contrasts against `Luciferase` are limited by the 5 independent physical
brains available (df ≈ 4) and do not reach significance. WT-neighbor NSCs
(`inx2 (not clones)`) are statistically indistinguishable from the unrelated
WT baseline (`Luciferase`), while the clonal CI-RNAi NSCs (`inx2`)
proliferate significantly less than their WT neighbors in the same brain.

---

## Fig 4D & 4L: Glial RNAi screen (pooled analysis, joint BH-FDR)

EdU-positive progeny per NSC clone is compared across a pooled
set of glial RNAi knockdowns (the transmembrane-transporter and
metabolic-enzyme screens, Fig 4D and Fig 4L, plus the cortex-glia and
glial-OxPhos screen conditions). Each knockdown is compared against the shared
reference controls `mCherry x Luciferase` (wild-type proliferation) and
`ND42 x Luciferase` (Complex I dysfunction baseline), one clone per row.

Brains are the biological replicate and the model is:

`EdU ~ condition + (1 | brain_uid)`

Each knockdown is compared to `ND42 x Luciferase`, with a Benjamini-Hochberg
FDR correction applied jointly across all knockdown contrasts.

```{r}
#| label: combined-load-data
#| code-summary: "Load the pooled glial RNAi screen data"

CTRL_COMB <- "mCherry x Luciferase"
REF_COMB  <- "ND42 x Luciferase"

combined_raw <- read_stat("edu_glial_screen.csv") %>%
    filter(in_combined_screen, !is.na(value)) %>%
    transmute(
        EdU         = value,
        genotype    = genotype,
        date        = collection_date,
        brain_uid   = replicate_id,
        figure      = manuscript_panel,
        screen_type
    )
```

### Data Summary

```{r}
#| label: combined-data-summary
#| code-summary: "Summarise the screen: clones, conditions, knockdowns, brains, dates"
#| output: true

combined_raw %>%
    summarise(
        n_clone_rows = n(),
        n_conditions = n_distinct(genotype),
        n_knockdowns = n_distinct(genotype[screen_type != "control"]),
        n_brains = n_distinct(brain_uid),
        n_dates = n_distinct(date)
    ) %>%
    minimal_tbl()
```

### Statistical analysis

```{r}
#| label: combined-condition-factor
#| code-summary: "List the screen knockdowns and build the condition factor"
#| output: false

screen_kds <- combined_raw %>%
    filter(screen_type != "control") %>%
    pull(genotype) %>%
    unique() %>%
    sort()
n_screen_kds <- length(screen_kds)

combined_model_data <- combined_raw %>%
    mutate(
        condition = factor(
            genotype,
            levels = c(CTRL_COMB, REF_COMB, screen_kds)
        )
    )
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" collapse="true"}
## Replication counts per knockdown

```{r}
#| label: combined-replication-counts
#| output: true
#| echo: false

combined_model_data %>%
    filter(screen_type != "control") %>%
    group_by(figure, screen_type, condition) %>%
    summarise(
        n_clone_rows = n(),
        n_brains     = n_distinct(brain_uid),
        n_dates      = n_distinct(date),
        .groups      = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(figure, screen_type, condition) %>%
    minimal_tbl()
```

:::

### Diagnostics

```{r}
#| label: combined-screen-model
#| code-summary: "Fit combined-screen no-date model"

combined_screen_model <- lmerTest::lmer(
    EdU ~ condition + (1 | brain_uid),
    data = combined_model_data,
    REML = TRUE,
    control = lme4::lmerControl(
        optimizer = "bobyqa",
        optCtrl = list(maxfun = 200000)
    )
)

summary(combined_screen_model)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" collapse="true"}
## Model fit diagnostics with DHARMa

Scaled residuals from 1,000 simulations are tested for uniform distribution (Kolmogorov–Smirnov), dispersion, and an excess of outliers; all three should be non-significant for a well-fitting model.

```{r}
#| label: combined-dharma
#| code-summary: "Run DHARMa diagnostics"
#| output: true
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

sim_combined <- DHARMa::simulateResiduals(
    combined_screen_model,
    n = 1000,
    seed = DHARMA_SEED
)
plot(sim_combined)

invisible(capture.output(
    combined_dharma_tests <- list(
        uniformity     = DHARMa::testUniformity(sim_combined, plot = FALSE),
        dispersion     = DHARMa::testDispersion(sim_combined, plot = FALSE),
        outliers = DHARMa::testOutliers(sim_combined, plot = FALSE)
    )
))

combined_dharma_tests %>%
    purrr::map_dfr(
        \(t) tibble(statistic = t$statistic, p.value = t$p.value),
        .id = "test"
    ) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)), sig = sig_stars(p.value)) %>%
    minimal_tbl()
```

:::

```{r}
#| label: combined-random-effects
#| code-summary: "Variance-components table (between-brain vs. residual)"
#| output: true

vc_combined <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(combined_screen_model))
vc_combined$pct <- round(100 * vc_combined$vcov / sum(vc_combined$vcov), 1)

vc_combined[, c("grp", "vcov", "pct")] %>%
    minimal_tbl()
```

### Global F-test

Type III ANOVA F-test; the `condition` term tests whether any knockdown differs from the reference across the screen.

```{r}
#| label: combined-anova
#| code-summary: "Type III ANOVA"
#| output: true

combined_anova_res <- anova(combined_screen_model, type = "III", ddf = "Satterthwaite") %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("term") %>%
    rename(df_num = NumDF, df_den = DenDF, F = `F value`, p.value = `Pr(>F)`)

combined_anova_res %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)), sig = sig_stars(p.value)) %>%
    sig_tbl()
```

```{r}
#| label: combined-anova-stats
#| echo: false
#| output: false
comb_f    <- signif(combined_anova_res$F[1], 3)
comb_dfn  <- combined_anova_res$df_num[1]
comb_dfd  <- signif(combined_anova_res$df_den[1], 3)
comb_fp   <- fmt_p(combined_anova_res$p.value[1])
```

The `condition` term was highly significant ($F(`r comb_dfn`, `r comb_dfd`) = `r comb_f`$, $p = `r comb_fp`$); at least one knockdown condition differs from the CI dysfunction baseline.

### Each knockdown vs. ND42 x Luciferase (joint BH-FDR)

Estimates are in EdU percentage points. The phenotype contrast
(`ND42 x Luciferase` vs. `mCherry x Luciferase`) is a single comparison and is
not corrected. Each knockdown is compared to `ND42 x Luciferase`, with a
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction applied jointly across all `r n_screen_kds`
knockdown contrasts.

```{r}
#| label: combined-emmeans
#| code-summary: "Estimated marginal means per condition"

combined_emmeans <- emmeans::emmeans(combined_screen_model, specs = ~ condition)
summary(combined_emmeans)
```

```{r}
#| label: combined-phenotype-contrast
#| code-summary: "CI dysfunction vs. wild-type phenotype contrast (uncorrected)"
#| output: true

phenotype_contrast_comb <- emmeans::contrast(
    combined_emmeans,
    method = list(
        "ND42 x Luciferase - mCherry x Luciferase" =
            c(-1, 1, rep(0, length(screen_kds)))
    ),
    adjust = "none"
)

phenotype_contrast_summary <- summary(phenotype_contrast_comb, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)) %>%
    as_tibble()

phenotype_contrast_summary %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)), sig = sig_stars(p.value)) %>%
    sig_tbl()
```

```{r}
#| label: combined-phenotype-stats
#| echo: false
#| output: false
pheno_est <- signif(phenotype_contrast_summary$estimate[1], 3)
pheno_t   <- signif(phenotype_contrast_summary$t.ratio[1], 3)
pheno_df  <- signif(phenotype_contrast_summary$df[1], 3)
pheno_p   <- fmt_p(phenotype_contrast_summary$p.value[1])
```

The CI dysfunction baseline (`ND42 x Luciferase`) showed a `r abs(pheno_est)` EdU pp reduction relative to wild-type ($t(`r pheno_df`) = `r pheno_t`$, $p = `r pheno_p`$).

```{r}
#| label: combined-screen-contrasts
#| code-summary: "Each knockdown vs. ND42 x Luciferase; joint Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across knockdowns"
#| output: true

combined_em_screen <- combined_emmeans[
    match(c(REF_COMB, screen_kds), combined_emmeans@grid$condition)
]

combined_screen_contrasts <- summary(
    emmeans::contrast(
        combined_em_screen,
        method = "trt.vs.ctrl",
        ref = 1,
        adjust = "none"
    ),
    infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)
) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    mutate(
        gene = as.character(contrast) %>%
            str_remove(fixed(paste0(" - ", REF_COMB))) %>%
            str_remove(fixed(paste0(" / ", REF_COMB))) %>%
            str_replace("^\\((.+)\\)$", "\\1"),
        p.fdr = p.adjust(p.value, method = "BH"),
        sig_label = sig_stars(p.fdr, na_as = NA_character_)
    )

genotype_figure <- combined_raw %>%
    filter(screen_type != "control") %>%
    distinct(genotype, figure, screen_type)

combined_results <- combined_screen_contrasts %>%
    left_join(genotype_figure, by = c("gene" = "genotype")) %>%
    select(
        figure,
        screen_type,
        gene,
        estimate,
        SE,
        df,
        lower.CL,
        upper.CL,
        t.ratio,
        p.value,
        p.fdr,
        sig_label
    ) %>%
    arrange(figure, p.fdr)

combined_results_display <- combined_results %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)))

reactable::reactable(
    combined_results_display,
    elementId     = "combined_screen_table",
    filterable    = TRUE,
    pagination    = FALSE,
    bordered      = TRUE,
    compact       = TRUE,
    highlight     = TRUE,
    defaultSorted = "p.fdr",
    theme = reactable::reactableTheme(
        borderColor    = "#dee2e6",
        stripedColor   = "#f8f9fa",
        highlightColor = "#f0f0f0",
        cellPadding    = "6px 8px",
        style          = list(fontSize = "0.9rem", fontFamily = "inherit")
    ),
    rowStyle = function(index) {
        sig   <- combined_results_display$sig_label[index]
        color <- switch(sig, "***" = "#c8e6c9", "**" = "#def0de", "*" = "#f0faf0", NA)
        if (!is.na(color)) list(backgroundColor = color) else list()
    },
    defaultColDef = reactable::colDef(
        header = function(value, name) {
            htmltools::tagList(
                value,
                htmltools::tags$span(
                    "⇅",
                    title = "Click to sort",
                    style = "margin-left: 4px; color: #999; font-size: 0.75em; font-weight: normal;"
                )
            )
        }
    ),
    columns = list(
        figure      = reactable::colDef(minWidth = 70),
        screen_type = reactable::colDef(
            name     = "Type",
            minWidth = 90,
            filterInput = function(values, name) {
                htmltools::tags$select(
                    style = "width: 100%; max-width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box;",
                    onchange = sprintf(
                        "Reactable.setFilter('combined_screen_table', '%s', event.target.value || undefined)",
                        name
                    ),
                    htmltools::tags$option(value = "", "All"),
                    lapply(sort(unique(values)), htmltools::tags$option)
                )
            }
        ),
        gene      = reactable::colDef(minWidth = 145),
        estimate  = reactable::colDef(minWidth = 85),
        SE        = reactable::colDef(minWidth = 48),
        df        = reactable::colDef(minWidth = 48),
        lower.CL  = reactable::colDef(name = "Lower", minWidth = 65),
        upper.CL  = reactable::colDef(name = "Upper", minWidth = 65),
        t.ratio   = reactable::colDef(minWidth = 54),
        p.value   = reactable::colDef(minWidth = 70),
        p.fdr     = reactable::colDef(minWidth = 70),
        sig_label = reactable::colDef(name = "Sig.",  minWidth = 55)
    )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: combined-sig-count
#| echo: false
#| output: false
n_sig_combined <- sum(combined_results$p.fdr < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
```

`r n_sig_combined` of `r n_screen_kds` knockdowns reached BH-FDR < 0.05 relative to the CI dysfunction baseline.
